articles.headlineJa: NFL第2週ハイライト：ベストプレー、名シーン、タッチダウンなど
articles.descriptionJa: スーパープレーのタッチダウンや必見のプレーなど、NFL第2週の厳選された名シーンをチェックしましょう。
articles.body:
There are eight games during Sunday's early window in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season, and we have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

Sunday's slate includes two key divisional games: From the NFC North, the Minnesota Vikings, with Carson Wentz starting under center, visit the unbeaten Chicago Bears, and in the NFC South, the Carolina Panthers play at the Atlanta Falcons, who will have Cooper Rush at QB again. Elsewhere, QB Joe Burrow will be managing back tightness as his Cincinnati Bengals go up against one of the NFL's best defenses in the Houston Texans.

Be sure to check here for the top plays from Sunday, and keep this file bookmarked for when the slate of five afternoon games and the "Sunday Night Football" matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and the Kansas City Chiefs kicks off.

Week 2 highlights

articles.headline: Rangers put pitcher Quantrill on IL due to right lat tightness
articles.description: The Rangers put versatile right-hander Cal Quantrill on the 15-day injured list Sunday, a day after he exited following only four batters and 12 pitches because of right lat tightness.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- The AL West-leading Texas Rangers put versatile right-hander Cal Quantrill on the 15-day injured list Sunday, a day after he exited following only four batters and 12 pitches because of right lat tightness.

Hard-throwing right-hander Winston Santos was recalled from Triple-A Round Rock and joined the Rangers before the finale of their three-game series against Toronto.

About an hour before the game, the Rangers said right fielder Brandon Nimmo was being scratched from the starting lineup because of illness.

Before the IL move was announced, manager Skip Schumaker said the Rangers knew going into Saturday night's game that Quantrill's velocity was lower.

Quantrill (9-5) was showing no signs of pain when Schumaker, pitching coach Jordan Tiegs and head trainer Matt Lucero went to the mound in the second inning and he came out of the game. Quantrill has a 2.86 ERA in 32 games (15 starts) after going to spring training with the Rangers on a minor league deal.

He left his previous start after six innings and 70 pitches at Arizona last Sunday with back soreness.

Quantrill, 31, has a 1.75 ERA (11 earned runs in 56⅔ innings) over his past 11 appearances (10 starts). Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees at 1.64 is the only qualified pitcher with a better ERA over that span.

Santos is beginning his third stint with the Rangers, though his only appearance in the first two was his big league debut on July 1 at Cleveland, where he allowed two runs in two innings. He has 103 strikeouts in 83⅓ innings in the minor leagues this season.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by George Pickens and Jayden Daniels
articles.description: Rounding up all top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
articles.body:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals' defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

The source was cornerback DJ Turner II's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

"I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king. This Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

Sunday afternoon arrivals

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens kept it simple up top, with a pop of color below for his arrival ahead of a divisional game against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Pickens wore a solid black T-shirt, multi-colored striped shorts, and purple-and-black Nike Dunks on the feet.

Here are more notable arrivals from the 4 p.m. slate:

Best of 1 p.m. arrivals

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield was dressed to impress, arriving for a home game against his former team, the Cleveland Browns. Mayfield wore a cream polo with khaki and green striped and white shoes.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson wore a red letterman jacket and loose-fit khaki pants ahead of a road matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Here are some of the other memorable fits from Sunday's 1 p.m. slate:

Thursday night's best fit

To kick off Week 2, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb arrived in a plaid Archival button-down shirt paired with dark denim jeans.

articles.headline: Gary Neville explains 'worst 15 minutes' Manchester United claim
articles.description: Gary Neville branded Manchester United's early second-half display against Fulham as the worst he had seen in more than 45 years.
articles.body:
Gary Neville branded Manchester United's early second-half display against Fulham as the worst he had seen in more than 45 years.

United were fortunate to leave Craven Cottage with a 1-1 draw after Matheus Cunha's late deflected effort snatched a point, but they had earlier gifted the hosts a comical own goal from Lisandro Martínez.

It came in the 63rd minute, capping a lethargic, error-strewn start to the half, and the goal felt fittingly surreal, Senne Lammens fumbling a tame shot with his legs and Martinez then tucked the ball past him as the goalkeeper struggled to find his balance.

During Sky Sports' coverage former United defender Neville described that period of the match as "absolutely pathetic."

"I've watched Man United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen," Neville said.

"Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort. What must [Michael] Carrick be thinking?"

Neville later explained his stance: "I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I have never seen Manchester United walk as much as that.

"Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he's defending them, he is loyal and wants his players to work for him. There is a long way left in the season.

"I called them mannequins. I have never seen a Manchester United team, for 15 minutes, walk around as much as that. No alerts, not on your toes, you should always be on your toes, there was no shifting up two or three yards. Just walking when Fulham were in possession.

"There needs to be a rebalance. I wish he could play the attacking players but they are going to kill him defensively."

Neville added: "Not running is the only thing that I will call a disgrace."

- Man United rescue draw at Fulham after own goal shocker

- Fulham 1-1 Man United result: As it happened

A draw left United without a win in three Premier League games and means they will spend the international break in the bottom half of the table.

United made it their joint-lowest points return after five matches in the Premier League after failing to beat Fulham, previously set in 2014-15. That season under Louis van Gaal saw the team win only one of those opening five, 4-0 at home to QPR, although they recovered well and went on to finish fourth.

Press Association contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Why no Man United penalty at Fulham?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Should Man United have gotten a penalty at Fulham?

Fulham 1-1 Man United (Sept. 20)

Referee: Peter Bankes

VAR: Nick Hopton

Time: 86 minutes

Incident: Possible penalty to Man United for a handball

What happened: Man United's Lisandro Martínez felt he should have earned a penalty when he fired the ball at Fulham defender Calvin Bassey from close range and the ball struck Bassey's arm. The referee did not feel it was an offence and waved away the appeals for a penalty.

VAR decision: VAR agreed with the referee's interpretation of the incident, that the ball was struck at close range, defenders' arms were close to his body and within bodyline and therefore not a handball offence. VAR checked and cleared the on-filed decision as correct.

Verdict and insight: While Man United might have wanted the penalty, this was a correct on-field decision by the refereeing team and non-intervention by VAR.

This incident is a good example of how the handball law can create confusion in these types of situations. When the ball is struck at close range, the law is clear that the referee should allow play to continue if the player's hand or arm movement is the result of a natural reflex to potentially protect the player's face, and if such action does not make their body unnaturally bigger.

Additionally, if arms are within the body line and the ball would have struck the body/face this should also be taken into consideration when applying this law.

Bassey's reaction falls within this interpretation and was a good read by the on-field assistant referee, who would have led the communication in this incident.

Was Rice lucky not to be sent off at Brighton?

Brighton & Hove Albion 3-0 Arsenal (Sept. 19)

Referee: Darren England

VAR: Tim Wood

Time: 90 + 7 mins

Incident: Possible red card for Arsenal's Declan Rice

What happened: Rice picked up a late yellow card when he appeared to kick out at Brighton's Malick Yalcouyé in an off-the-ball incident.

VAR decision: The on-field decision of yellow card was checked and cleared as correct by the VAR.

articles.headline: Patriots starting RG Mike Onwenu carted off with ankle injury
articles.description: Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field with an ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field late in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the team quickly ruled him out with a right ankle injury.

The injury came on a play when quarterback Drake Maye was sacked, and Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt landed on the back of Onwenu's legs.

Onwenu is a seven-year veteran who has the longest tenure with the Patriots after being selected in the sixth round of the 2020 draft.

Durability has been one of his calling cards, as Sunday marked his 100th career regular-season game and 92nd start. A University of Michigan alum, he also has played in five playoff games (four starts).

Onwenu, 28, is in the final year of his contract in 2026.

Veteran Greg Van Roten, whom the Patriots signed to a one-year, $3 million deal on Aug. 18, took over for Onwenu.
